result.title: ECGJev: Question-Conditioned Option Scoring for 12-Lead ECG Interpretation
result.comment: 5 pages (4 pages plus ethics statement and references), 2 figures. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027. Zhuoyuan Li and Xidong Wu contributed equally
result.summary: Clinical interpretation of a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) often requires answering targeted diagnostic questions with clear, quantifiable decisions. We introduce ECGJev, the first ECG framework built on a decision decoder, a pretrained language model trained to return a probability for every listed option. A question-conditioned bridge compresses frozen waveform and spectrogram features into 16 ECG tokens, and a two-stage procedure adapts the bridge and low-rank adapters on the decoder's native option readout using diagnostic labels alone, scoring all options for a question in one forward pass. Evaluated across four ECG benchmarks, ECGJev achieves the highest macro-F1 on CPSC2018 (80.46%), PTB-XL (71.68%) and Chapman (96.86%), and generalizes competitively to the small-sample PTB cohort. Concept probes and perturbation analyses further show that its predictions rely directly on the ECG input, remain stable under option-order and wording variations, and transfer zero-shot to unseen waveform concepts. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhuoyuanli-lab/ECGJev.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ECGJev：将冻结的 12 导联心电波形与频谱特征经问题条件桥压缩为 16 个 token，再由预训练决策解码器一次前向为所有候选选项打分，并在四个 ECG 基准上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「少量 token 压缩 + 选项式读出 + 扰动与探针检验预测是否依赖输入」的组合，可供核查 LVR 中答案是否真正使用 latent 内容及证据归因问题，但属跨领域线索，迁移价值需人工判断。
